To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the impact-parameter dependence of the non-diffractively produced leading particles is in good qualitative agreement, for a sample of annhilation and non-annhilation p p collisions at 5.7 GeV/c, with the basic requirement for a parton cluster model of hadron collisions, namely that the non-difractive cross-sections for the production of leading particles should be proportional to the impact parameter squared.
the impact parameter dependence of the leading particle production in non-diffrative pp collisions at 200 GeV/c is very similar for the leading particles with different quantum numbers.

the model of hadron collisions proposed by us is able to describe the main experimental features of the leading particles, including their impact parameter angular distributions and their angular distributions in the c.m. system, in a qualitative way.

we have found a model for the structure and collisions of hadrons which is consistent with a large number of experimental data.

the parton-cluster model is in good qualitative agreement both with the data and with other theoretical models of hadron collisions, but that it is not yet in a position to make quantitative predictions for the impact parameter distribution of non-difffractive collisions.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the model of hadron collisions based on the parton-cluster picture of hadrons provides a good qualitative description of the experimental data on non-diffracted hadron interactions.
hadron structure and the impact parameter structure of hadron collisions can be understood in terms of a very simple parton-cluster model of a hadron.

the impact parameter dependence of the cross sections is not a simple exponential, as is usually assumed, but has an oscillatory behavior, which is in qualitative agreement with the parton-cluster model of non-difrractive collisions.
